<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → `packageMentionDocs`.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b00e8b53c31815e5a4fb3d21282f5176ab98c422 && git checkout b00e8b53c31815e5a4fb3d21282f5176ab98c422
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable

```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87af66e5b6c75af7989ecbdc8820f1ca4a66596a` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Final head for review: `275dd464`. CI is green on it: every check run on the head is success or an expected skip, with none failed or pending, including all 16 Test UI and 10 Test Core shards.

Since the PR opened, `275dd464` adds a module-top `import '@objectstack/metadata'` to the new runtime pin (`automation-resume-screen-input-fields-37526.test.ts`), as `check:test-source-alias` prescribed. The dispatcher's reach loads it lazily, so the first load is now paid at collection and not inside a case's timeout. The red runs on `cffcc03c` were that gate plus lanes cancelled by the push.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `275dd464efd6bf1b7b0acdf42afe759ce2bbedf6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/flowResponse.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx

First round. Read: card #37526 with its two comments, the PR body and its two comments, the 25-file net diff against `main`, and the 70 check-runs on the head (each `success` or `skipped`; none red, none pending). The tests, the changeset text, the two docs pages and the eleven locale files are outside this scope and stay with the lane seat's ACCEPT; the locale files and the docs pages were read only to answer ③.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of the resume route: unchanged.** `validateScreenInputs` (`screen-input-contract.ts`) is not in the diff. The engine hunk adds one member to a refusal it already returned; no refusal is added and none is removed. Right.
- **`AutomationResult.fields?: FieldError[]`**: a new optional member on a published contract interface. Additive for every implementer and every reader of `IAutomationService`. Right, a widening.
- **`TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data.fields`**: `z.array(FieldErrorSchema).optional()`, the Zod mirror that the compile-time identity `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` (`automation-api.zod.test.ts:55`) requires. `TypeScript Type Check` is green on the head, so the two sides are the same type. No route serves the member inside `data`: a screen refusal is a resume answer and leaves as a 400. That is the standing shape of this schema (the resume-refusal members of `code` are mirrored the same way), and the describe says where a transport serves it. Right.
- **Wire**: `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` gains `error.details.fields` at both doors `classifyResumeResult` feeds, the REST resume arm (`automation.ts:5050`) and MCP `resume_run` (`mcp.ts:2822`). `splitSemanticCode` (`error-envelope.ts:100`) promotes `code` and leaves the rest, so the envelope reads `details: { fields }`, and with no findings it carries no `details`, as on `main`. `error.code`, `error.message`, the status and the six other rows are unchanged. Right, a widening.
- **One derived widening the PR does not name**: `@objectstack/client` already lifts `error.details.fields` onto the error it throws (`packages/client/src/index.ts:8685`), so SDK callers now get `err.fields` on this refusal. No byte of that package moves, so it owes no changeset entry. Right.
- **Console**: the dialog's `required` check now refuses a string that is empty once trimmed. `isUnanswered` is the exact negation of the engine's `isPresent` (`screen-input-contract.ts:58`). It changes what the dialog sends, never what the route accepts. Right.
- **Metadata protocol**: no authorable key, accepted value or metadata type changes. `ScreenFieldSpec` and the flow schemas are untouched, and both spec members are response-side. `Metadata-protocol: none` holds.
- **Generated output**: the one regenerated row in `content/docs/references/api/automation-api.mdx` carries the new describe; `check:docs` rides `TypeScript Type Check`, green.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/37526-screen-required-whitespace.md` takes `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`: the five packages whose source the diff moves, and no sixth package's source moves. A non-protocol widening ships `patch` (AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist 3). Matches.
- The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line stands at the start of a line on the PR body and in the changeset, and it holds: the published surface grows by one optional member, declared twice, and nothing narrows.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` stands on both carriers and holds (①).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev flag, PR body *Small decisions* 1.** The claim on the card promised `details.issues` entries of `field` and `code` with no message; the PR serves `details.fields` entries of `{ field, code, message }`. Answered, accepted. `fields` is the name ADR-0114 D4 fixed for this slot; `FieldErrorSchema` requires `message`; an English producer line in the same slot has precedent on `main` (the flow-definition door, `automation.ts:4318`). Each `message` is a substring of the unchanged `error.message`, so no string reaches the wire that the same response did not already carry. `FieldErrorSchema.message` describes itself as rendered in the caller's locale; the new member's describe says outright that this producer's line is English, so the member is accurate where the element's general describe is not. The Console drops `message` (`screenInputFindings` keeps `field` and `code`), which is what holds the card's second acceptance line.
- **Dev flag, *Small decisions* 2** (a bound finding reads the limit off the screen field's own `min` / `max`). Answered, holds. The engine raises `min_value` / `max_value` only off a numeric `min` / `max` on the served screen field, the same field spec the dialog renders, so the fall-back to `flowRunner.fieldNotAccepted` is reached only against a spec that lacks the bound.
- **Dev flag, *Small decisions* 3** (toast kept beside the banner). UI behaviour with no contract effect; the lane seat's.
- **PR comment 7199609005's face list** (`details.fields`, `AutomationResult.fields` with its Zod mirror, the regenerated page): complete for the spec. The SDK effect in ① is the one addition.
- **Docs.** Of the six hand-written pages the docs-drift advisory names, `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` is the one that describes this refusal; its new paragraph agrees with the runtime. The other five state nothing this diff makes false. Prose faces, left to the lane seat.
- **Locale keys.** The dialog reads `flowRunner.invalidScreenInput`, `flowRunner.fieldNotAccepted`, `validation.required`, `validation.min` and `validation.max`. All eleven locale files carry all five, the two new ones inside `flowRunner`, with the `{{field}}` / `{{min}}` / `{{max}}` slots the calls pass.
- `open_questions`: none on the card or the PR.
- SQL push-down: the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no note owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`** holds against the code it describes:

- the six codes it lists are the six `validateScreenInputs` raises, no more and no fewer;
- "Set with that code only": the one producer is `refuseInvalidScreenInput` (`engine.ts:9621-9631`), returned as it is by `run-resume.ts:1694`, and the door serves the member under that code alone (`automation.ts:3708`);
- "A transport serves it as `error.details.fields`": both doors do, through the one table;
- "`error` keeps the whole sentence": the sentence is untouched.

**`packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts`** holds: the element is `FieldErrorSchema`, the identity pin binds it to the contract, and its first consumer (`screenInputFindings`, then `screenInputFieldErrors`) reads exactly `field` and `code`. The new runtime pin parses the served envelope under `ApiErrorSchema` and each entry under `FieldErrorSchema`.

**Implementing files** agree with the contract: `engine.ts` copies each finding's three members and adds none; `automation.ts` serves them under the one code and only when the list is non-empty; `flowResponse.ts` and `FlowRunner.tsx` place by `field` and `code` and never render `message`.

Tried to break it, and it held:

- a result carrying `fields` under another code is not served;
- an empty list serves no `details`;
- two findings for one field: the dialog keeps the first;
- a finding for a field that is not on screen (an undeclared key, a field hidden on the client): banner only, no field marked;
- a server that serves no findings: `[]`, the catalog banner;
- the client's and the engine's presence predicates: identical, for strings, `null`, `undefined`, `false` and `0`.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — "one entry per violated field" (the contract jsdoc and the schema describe, and from there the reference page, `flows.mdx` and the changeset) is one entry per finding. A `record_link` field declared `required` and sent `null` gets `required` and `invalid_value`; a field declared with `min` above `max` can get both bounds. And for `unknown_field`, `field` is the key the caller sent, not a screen field's `name`. No code reads the sentence, and the Console handles both cases. Accepted deviation on this head: a describe fix moves a reviewed file and its generated page. Fold it into the next edit of that jsdoc.

N2 (nit) — the jsdoc on `ScreenInputIssue.code` (`screen-input-contract.ts:44-46`, outside the diff) still says these codes "ride inside the refusal's message"; with the engine hunk they ride `fields`. Comment only; same follow-up as N1.

Reviewed-by: `session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA`

**VERDICT: PASS**
